title: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD)
lead: Pulmonary rehabilitation is one of the most effective treatments in all of medicine for breathless patients.
case: A 66-year-old ex-smoker (45 pack-years) with COPD, mMRC 3, walks 260 m in 6MWT with SpO2 falling from 93% to 85% on room air, Borg 6. Two admissions this year. Goal: walk to the market.

differentials.name: Asthma
differentials.key: Variable symptoms, younger onset, reversible airflow

differentials.name: Bronchiectasis
differentials.key: Large daily sputum volumes, recurrent infections

differentials.name: Interstitial lung disease
differentials.key: Fine crackles, restrictive pattern, desaturation on exertion

qa: Can he start pulmonary rehabilitation? Yes, after medical review of oxygen needs during exercise because he desaturates.
What starting intensity would you choose? Walking at about 60 to 80% of his 6MWT speed or at Borg 3 to 4, with intervals and supplemental oxygen as prescribed.
Why include arm training? Unsupported arm activities cause disproportionate breathlessness.
What breathing technique helps him on stairs? Pursed-lip breathing and "blow as you go" pacing.
What does an mMRC of 3 mean? He stops for breath after about 100 metres or a few minutes on level ground.

redFlags.Finding: Acute severe breathlessness, unable to speak, confusion, drowsiness
redFlags.Immediate action: Emergency team; controlled oxygen to prescribed target

redFlags.Finding: SpO2 persistently below target during exercise despite rest

manual.name: Breathing control
manual.finding: Relaxed shoulders, gentle tidal breathing through the nose, using the lower chest

manual.name: Pursed-lip breathing
manual.finding: Breathe in through the nose, out slowly through lips shaped as if whistling, exhale about twice as long as inhale

manual.name: Positions of ease
manual.finding: Forward lean sitting with forearms on thighs or a table; forward lean standing against a wall

manual.name: Active cycle of breathing techniques (ACBT)
manual.finding: Breathing control, then 3 to 4 deep breaths with a hold, then breathing control, then huffs (medium then short), repeat

manual.name: Positive expiratory pressure (PEP) or oscillating PEP devices
manual.finding: 10 to 15 breaths through the device, then huffs

manual.name: Paced breathing with activity
manual.finding: "Blow as you go": exhale during the effort

exercise.Prescription: 3 to 5 days a week; start about 60 to 80% of 6MWT walking speed, or at Borg dyspnoea 3 to 4; 20 to 30 min total, intervals allowed
exercise.Progress when: Borg falls below 3 at the same workload
Patients too breathless for continuous work

exercise.Prescription: Major muscle groups, especially quadriceps; 2 to 3 sets of 8 to 12 reps at a load that is moderately hard
Unsupported arm exercises (arm activities are very breathless for COPD patients)
Consider if inspiratory muscles are weak [Ref – to verify]
Self-management, medication and inhaler technique, exacerbation action plan, energy conservation, smoking cessation

exerciseNotes: Program length is typically 6 to 12 weeks, at least twice weekly supervised [Ref – to verify]. Maintenance exercise afterwards is essential.
modalityNotes: Supplemental oxygen during exercise for those who desaturate, as prescribed. Non-invasive ventilation during training only in specialist settings. Neuromuscular electrical stimulation for very weak, deconditioned patients who cannot exercise [Ref – to verify].
pathway: Optimise breathing techniques and airway clearance.
Maintenance: home exercise, community classes, self-management plan.
Early return to rehabilitation after exacerbations.
